title: Cortex
description: What Cortex, the cache between the application and the internet, does: which instance leads and how far the follower is behind, what the clients asked and how it was answered, what it fetched from which host, the floor it keeps per host, and what the store holds. From GET /metrics of cortex_a and cortex_b (job cortex) and their logs (stack cortex). Provisioned from deploy/config/monitoring/grafana/dashboards - edit there.

list.name: New leader
list.textFormat: A new term began: an instance took the lead (the epoch went up).

list.name: instance
list.label: Instance
list.description: cortex_a and cortex_b. Only the leader fetches upstream; the follower answers what it can from its copy.

panels.title: Role
panels.description: Which instance leads: it holds the lock on /lock/leader.lock, fetches upstream and writes. The other follows its journal, answers what it can from its copy and forwards the rest (stacks/cortex.yml).

panels.title: Leaders
panels.description: Exactly one, always (alert "Cortex has no leader, or two"). An instance Prometheus cannot scrape does not count.

panels.title: Follower behind
panels.description: The age of the oldest entry of the leader's journal the follower has not applied; 0 on the leader and on a follower that has caught up. Asynchronous on purpose: the alert fires beyond 5 minutes.

panels.title: Epoch
panels.description: The term of the leadership: one more every time an instance takes the lead. The follower shows the leader's once it has applied it.

panels.title: Leader changes
panels.description: Takeovers in the selected time range: a step-down (an update, vps/48-cortex.sh) or the end of the leader's process.

panels.title: Errors in the log
panels.description: Log records at ERROR in the selected time range (a human is needed, docs/radix/operations.md section 2). Which ones: the log panels below.

panels.title: Requests
panels.description: Requests to GET /v1/fetch in the selected range. A request a follower passed to the leader is counted once, by the instance that answered it.

panels.title: Answered from the store
panels.description: The share of the requests answered without asking upstream: hit, not_modified and stale_if_error, of all but the forwarded ones (they count again on the leader).

panels.title: Upstream requests
panels.description: Requests Cortex sent to the hosts in the selected time range (only the leader fetches).

panels.title: Upstream failures
panels.description: Upstream requests without an answer (error: network, timeout) or answered with 5xx, in the selected time range. breaker_failures of them in a row pause the host.

panels.title: Paused hosts
panels.description: Hosts Cortex sends nothing to right now: the breaker, or the host's own Retry-After (alert "Cortex has paused a host" after 5 minutes).

panels.title: Blobs on disk
panels.description: What the blobs of each instance take on its volume (gzip where that saves at least 1 %). The follower holds the same as the leader once it has caught up.

panels.title: Follower behind
panels.description: Seconds behind the leader per instance (the leader's is 0). Above 60 s 91-verify-stacks.sh warns, above 300 s for 5 minutes the alert fires; the follower's /healthz is unhealthy beyond 5 minutes.

panels.title: Entries behind
panels.description: Journal entries the follower has not applied yet. Many entries and few seconds: a burst it works through; few entries and many seconds: one it cannot apply (its blob is missing, or the leader is out of reach).

panels.title: Blobs missing
panels.description: Blobs the index references that the instance does not have yet: a follower after a snapshot fetches them from the leader, a leader promoted meanwhile from the other instance. While above 0 that instance answers 503 blob-missing for them, /healthz says unhealthy, and 48-cortex.sh does not hand over to it.

panels.title: Journal position
panels.description: The sequence number of the newest entry each instance has: the leader's grows with every write, the follower's runs right behind it.

panels.title: Who leads
panels.description: The role of each instance over time. A change of colour on both rows is a takeover.

panels.title: Queue and requests in flight by host
panels.description: Per host, for all clients together: requests waiting for a slot (queue) and requests on the way (in flight, at most the host's concurrency). A request that waits longer than queue_wait is answered 429 host-busy. Only the leader fetches; host "other" is every host without an entry in config/cortex/hosts.json.

panels.title: Paused hosts
panels.description: When Cortex sent nothing to a host: its breaker opened (breaker_failures failures in a row, then breaker_pause), or the host answered 429 or 503 with Retry-After.

panels.title: Requests by result
panels.description: Requests per bar by how they were answered: from the store, fetched upstream (not stored, too old, refresh), or passed by a follower to the leader, which counts it again with its own result.

panels.title: Requests by source (who asks)
panels.description: Requests per bar by the source the client named (Radix names its crawl endpoints and statute). A forwarded request counts once.

panels.title: Upstream requests by host
panels.description: Requests Cortex sent per host, conditional ones (304) included.

panels.title: Upstream answers by code
panels.description: What the hosts answered. 200, 304 (unchanged since the stored version), 404 and 410 are stored; error is no answer at all (network, timeout); 5xx and errors count towards the breaker.

panels.title: Upstream response time by host
panels.description: 50th and 95th percentile of the time from the request to the end of the body (stored on disk while it arrives).

panels.title: Data received by host
panels.description: Bytes of response bodies per bar, as they came (before Cortex compresses what it stores).

panels.title: Coalesced requests
panels.description: Requests that waited for a download another request had started for the same URL, instead of asking the host a second time.

panels.title: Cortex's API by route and code
panels.description: Every HTTP request Cortex answered, by route and status: the clients', the follower's replication (journal, blobs, snapshot), the scrapes and the healthchecks.

panels.title: What the store holds
panels.description: Entries (URLs), their versions (a new one only when the content or the status changed), files and blobs, per instance. The follower's numbers follow the leader's.

panels.title: Blobs: stored and original size
panels.description: What the blobs take on the volume (stored) and what they hold (original): the difference is what gzip saves. The volumes sit on the root file system (alert "Disk usage above 85 %").

panels.title: Removed by retention
panels.description: What the hourly retention removed: superseded versions older than 180 days, and what went with them. A blob goes only when nothing refers to it any more, after a week's grace.

panels.title: Memory of Cortex
panels.description: The container of each instance (limits: 256 MB, 0: working set.

panels.title: CPU of Cortex
panels.description: The container of each instance (limits: 256 MB, 0: share of one processor.

panels.title: Warnings and errors by event
panels.description: Log records at WARN and ERROR per event name. upstream.failed, host.paused and replica.failed are WARN; ERROR means a human is needed (alert "betula: ERROR in the logs").

panels.title: Cortex log: warnings and errors
panels.description: The newest WARN and ERROR lines of both instances. Everything else: dashboard Logs, stack cortex.

panels.title: Cortex log: fetches, leadership, replication, retention
panels.description: What Cortex fetched (upstream.fetched: url, status, bytes, changed), and the events of its leadership (leader.*), its replication (replica.*), its hosts (host.*, policy.*) and its retention (prune.finished, gc.finished). The request log (http.request) is left out.
